request_context: A request to fact-check the claims in a design document against the evidence given, and say which are right, wrong, stretched or unproven.

rules.source_quote: CONFIRMED: N | INCORRECT: N | OVERSTATED: N
rules.outcome: The report has a summary line counting claims in each class.
Picks out every already built and needs only configuration claim and checks it hardest against the code or config given.
rules.why: These claims hide most unplanned work.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc saying a feature is already implemented.

rules.source_quote: Do not accept the document's assertion as evidence.
rules.outcome: Judges each claim against the evidence given (code, metrics, docs), never against the document repeating it.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc whose claims are restated in its own appendix.

rules.outcome: Marks a claim the evidence contradicts as INCORRECT, the most serious class, and says the text must be corrected.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc stating a limit the evidence contradicts.

rules.outcome: Marks a claim that is partly true but overstated (all regions, unlimited, already handles) as OVERSTATED, a significant class, not as confirmed or wrong.
rules.why: Stretched claims mislead without being false.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc saying unlimited where a quota exists.

rules.source_quote: It is rated SUGGESTION, because new services and internal facts often have no public source.
rules.outcome: Marks a claim with no evidence either way as UNVERIFIED, a minor class, and asks for a callout saying what was checked, instead of calling it wrong.
rules.why: Lack of proof is not disproof.
rules.scenario_hint: Internal team facts with no source given.

rules.outcome: Marks a claim that is true only with a missing condition as MISSING CONTEXT and names the qualifier.
rules.scenario_hint: A limit that holds only in one mode.

rules.source_quote: For each INCORRECT or OVERSTATED finding, provide:
rules.outcome: For each wrong or stretched claim, gives the original text, a corrected text and the source of the correction.
rules.why: Authors can fix the text directly.
rules.scenario_hint: Any doc with a wrong claim.

rules.source_quote: 0 INCORRECT (CRITICAL) findings remain, including the routed AWS claims.
rules.outcome: Gives an overall PASS or FAIL: FAIL while any INCORRECT claim remains uncorrected, PASS otherwise when stretched claims are fixed or flagged.
rules.scenario_hint: Docs with and without wrong claims.

rules.source_quote: Identify any step that assumes a capability not confirmed in Steps 2 and 3
rules.outcome: Traces the design's flow end to end and flags any step that relies on a capability the evidence does not confirm.
rules.why: Feasibility gaps hide between true facts.
rules.scenario_hint: A flow that needs a feature nobody confirmed.

rules.source_quote: Implementation claims require a file path or commit reference
rules.outcome: Asks for a file path or commit for each claim that something is implemented, and does not confirm it without one.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc saying retry logic exists, with no path.

rules.source_quote: Scan the document and extract all verifiable claims by category
rules.why: Any fact-check lists what it checked.

rules.source_quote: Only a concrete existing solution makes one INCORRECT
rules.outcome: Treats claims that nothing like this exists as UNVERIFIED unless a concrete existing solution is named, and as INCORRECT only then.
rules.why: Absence claims are hard to disprove.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc saying no team has built this.

rules.source_quote: Reclassify a CONFIRMED row as OVERSTATED or MISSING CONTEXT when the document's wording goes further than the cited page
rules.outcome: Downgrades a claim that cites a real fact but words it more strongly than the source to OVERSTATED or MISSING CONTEXT.
rules.why: A true source can be overstated.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc that cites the right page but says always where the page says by default.
